title: A Asset for the Debt
premise: Freya Halloran, a whistle-blower who has survived twelve years under four assumed names, receives a call on a burner phone that should be dead — the voice belongs to Marcus Vane, the handler who once burned him and vanished. Vane offers a trade: extract Ilse Brandt, a defector carrying proof of a private intelligence network's crimes, and Freya gets the file that will finally clear his name. But every step of the extraction feels staged, and Freya realizes Brandt may be bait in a trap designed to flush out every ghost the network ever created. In the end Freya chooses justice over survival, exposing the network at devastating personal cost — Vane dies buying him the chance, and Freya walks into custody as a free man for the first time in twelve years.
about_author: Felix Montrose is the pen name of a former financial-crimes investigator who spent a decade inside compliance departments before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences from a coastal town he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Living quietly in Rotterdam as 'Daniel Reeve,' Freya follows his rigid survival rituals — cash only, no patterns, no past. A routine check reveals someone has queried his old case number. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of a man who knows it never lasts.

chapters.title: A Phone That Should Be Dead
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A burner buried in his emergency kit — one he never activated — rings. The voice is Marcus Vane, his former handler, presumed dead for nine years. Vane offers the file that can clear Freya's name if he extracts defector Ilse Brandt from Tallinn within six days. Beat: dread and temptation entwined.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV Freya, with a flashback to the original whistle-blowing that destroyed his career. He maps what he knows about the Meridian Network, the private intelligence firm he exposed and that apparently survived him. Beat: rage rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Archive
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Brandt. In a Tallinn safe flat, Ilse reviews encrypted files she stole from Meridian, aware she is being hunted. She trusts no one — least of all whoever her contact sends. Beat: cold competence masking terror.

chapters.title: Crossing the Gulf
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Traveling under name three, he makes contact with an old fixer, Lena Kask, who agrees to help but warns him the job smells engineered. First surveillance tail appears. Beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: POV Freya and Ilse alternating. Freya reaches Ilse; she tests him with a question only his real identity could answer, then nearly kills him when the answer comes too easily. Beat: two professionals deciding whether to trust.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carries
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. She shows Freya fragments of the archive: Meridian didn't survive — it was absorbed by its clients, including the agency that once employed Vane. Beat: the scale of corruption revealed, hope curdling.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Planning the exfiltration route through Estonia to Finland. Lena discovers the safe house was leased eleven days ago — before Vane ever called. Beat: the trap hypothesis takes shape.

chapters.title: The Man Who Burned Me
chapters.summary: POV Freya, extended flashback to Vane's betrayal twelve years ago — how the file Freya leaked was used to bury four colleagues, two fatally. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Tallinn After Dark
chapters.summary: POV Freya and Ilse. First move toward the port goes wrong; a Meridian wet team hits them early. They escape through the Old Town tunnels, Ilse saving Freya's life. Beat: forced partnership forged in blood.

chapters.title: Lena's Price
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Lena reveals she was approached weeks ago by someone offering money for word of 'Daniel Reeve' — she refused, which means Meridian already suspected. Beat: loyalty tested, guilt surfaced.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse admits she may have been allowed to defect; her escape was too clean. She offers Freya an out: leave without her. He refuses. Beat: moral commitment over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Gulf of Finland
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Night crossing on a fishing boat, pursued by a coast guard cutter running Meridian protocols. They make Finnish waters but lose their boat and contact with Lena. Beat: exhaustion and mounting dread.

chapters.title: Helsinki Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Safe house in Helsinki; Freya decrypts more of Ilse's archive and finds his own name listed as an active Meridian asset — recruitment dated last month. Someone has been building a paper trail making him complicit. Beat: horror at being rewritten.

chapters.title: The Voice Again
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Vane calls: extraction window moved up, new rendezvous, and a warning that the team hunting them answers to someone inside Freya's old agency. Freya realizes Vane is feeding him true intel — or perfectly poisoned truth. Beat: whiplash between gratitude and suspicion.

chapters.title: Ilse's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. She reveals she knew Vane before — he ran her insertion into Meridian years ago. Everything converges: Vane built both of them, and this operation is his endgame against his own masters. Beat: betrayal reframed as design.

chapters.title: The Rendezvous
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Meeting Vane face to face in a Helsinki shipyard. Vane confirms the trap: Meridian let the extraction run to capture all three ghosts at once — but Vane turned the trap, planning to detonate the archive publicly. Beat: confrontation charged with twelve years of debt.

chapters.title: Everything Owed
chapters.summary: POV Freya and Ilse. Meridian's kill team arrives early; Vane holds the dock long enough for Freya and Ilse to reach the broadcast point, taking fatal wounds. His last words: 'Debt cleared.' Beat: catharsis through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. From a borrowed server room, they release the full archive — Meridian's client list, the falsified file against Freya, everything — simultaneously to forty journalists. Beat: the terrifying calm after the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Long Light
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Twenty-four hours of flight as the story breaks worldwide and Meridian's hunters are recalled. Freya and Ilse part ways; she returns to testify, he cannot yet. Beat: bittersweet separation, freedom half-tasted.

chapters.title: Halloran
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya surrenders himself at his old agency's door under his real name, carrying evidence of his innocence. Interrogation, verification, and the slow dismantling of the frame. Beat: reclaiming identity as an act of courage.

chapters.title: A Asset No Longer
chapters.summary: POV Freya, epilogue. Months later, cleared and unremarkable, Freya visits Vane's unmarked grave and burns his last alias documents. A new burner phone sits in his drawer, silent. Beat: hard-won peace, vigilance retained, the price of survival finally paid.
